Construct augmented reduced-form and first-stage signals

Source: R/score-clate.R
iv_augmented_signals.Rd

Constructs two aligned signals from externally supplied nuisance predictions. This interface fits no nuisance models.

Usage

iv_augmented_signals(
  Y,
  D,
  A,
  e,
  m_y0,
  m_y1,
  m_d0 = NULL,
  m_d1,
  clip = 1e-08,
  one_sided = FALSE,
  row_ids = NULL,
  training = "supplied"
)

Arguments

Y

Finite numeric outcome vector.

D

Numeric binary treatment vector (0/1).

A

Numeric binary instrument vector (0/1).

e

Instrument propensity predictions in \([0,1]\), before clipping.

m_y0, m_y1

Outcome predictions conditional on instrument arm 0 and 1.

m_d0, m_d1

Treatment predictions conditional on instrument arm 0 and 1, in \([0,1]\). m_d0 may be omitted only with one_sided = TRUE.

clip

Propensity clipping threshold in (0,0.5), with 1 - clip < 1 in double precision.

one_sided

Explicit structural restriction that treatment is impossible under instrument 0. Requires D <= A and zero m_d0 if supplied.

row_ids

Optional unique, nonmissing character or numeric row identities. These record alignment; a single ID vector cannot detect independently misordered prediction arrays.

training

Descriptive declaration: supplied, oracle, full_sample, oob or cross_fit. It is not verified from predictions.

Value

An iv_signals list with phi_y, phi_d, row_ids, propensity (raw, used, clipped), nuisance (m_y0, m_y1, m_d0, m_d1) and meta.

Details

For either response \(R\), the signal is $$\phi_R=m_{R1}-m_{R0}+A(R-m_{R1})/e -(1-A)(R-m_{R0})/(1-e).$$ Both responses use the same clipped propensity. Arm subscripts refer to instrument assignment, not treatment received. Treatment predictions are validated, not silently clipped. Outcomes and outcome predictions are not capped. Finite unbounded-outcome computations do not certify the bounded learner conditions of the affine inference theorem.

Individual first-stage signals can be negative even under one-sided compliance. They remain unchanged. The CLATE equation averages both signals before dividing; do not average observation-level signal ratios.

Examples

z <- iv_augmented_signals(
  Y = c(1, 2, 0, 3), D = c(0, 1, 0, 1), A = c(0, 1, 1, 1),
  e = rep(.5, 4), m_y0 = rep(1, 4), m_y1 = rep(2, 4),
  m_d1 = rep(.6, 4), one_sided = TRUE
)
z$phi_y
#> [1]  1  1 -3  3
z$phi_d
#> [1]  0.6  1.4 -0.6  1.4
